sentences.zh: 这是路易斯安那州什里夫波特一个下雨的周二早晨，我站在希望医疗诊所外面，这是路易斯安那州仅存的三家诊所之一。

sentences.en: It's got a sort of double-door vestibule.

sentences.en: And this clinic is at the center of a major Supreme Court case, and it involves a significant question that could put the clinic's future at risk.

sentences.en: Hi.

sentences.en: You too.

sentences.en: Certainly.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.zh: 我真为你们和凯利感到遗憾。

sentences.en: Tell me about you.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲你吧。

sentences.en: How did you find yourself here?

sentences.en: What's your background?
sentences.zh: 你的背景是什么？

sentences.en: That is a really long story.
sentences.zh: 那真的是一个很长的故事。

sentences.en: That's all right.

sentences.en: How long ago was that?
sentences.zh: 那是多久以前的事？

sentences.en: So that's...
sentences.zh: 所以那是……

sentences.en: I've been here for 27 years.
sentences.zh: 我在这里27年了。

sentences.en: 27 years.
Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Personally, I worked here for two months before I told my mom, and I was a divorced mom living at home with her.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我在这里工作了两个月才告诉妈妈，当时我是一个和她住在一起的离异单亲妈妈。

sentences.en: And she told me that at first, it made her nervous to tell her mom, she comes from a big Catholic family, what it was she was going to do for a living.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，起初把她的工作内容告诉妈妈让她感到紧张，她来自一个庞大的天主教家庭。

sentences.en: And I worked here for two months before I finally told her.
sentences.zh: 我在这里工作了两个月，最后才告诉她。

sentences.en: But when I told her, I said, you know, I'm counseling women, but I didn't tell you the whole story.
sentences.zh: 但当我告诉她时，我说，你知道的，我在为女性做咨询，但我没有把整件事告诉你。

sentences.en: And her response was, women have always had abortions, darling.
sentences.zh: 她的反应是，亲爱的，女人们一直都在堕胎。

sentences.en: They always will.
sentences.zh: 她们以后也总是会堕胎。

sentences.en: They need a safe place.
sentences.zh: 她们需要一个安全的地方。

sentences.en: And this is someone who...
sentences.zh: 而这个人……

sentences.en: Did that surprise you that you got that response?
sentences.zh: 听到这样的反应，你感到意外吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I had 15 siblings.
sentences.zh: 我有15个兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: To find my mom after all this was pro-choice.
sentences.zh: 经历这一切后，发现我妈妈竟然支持堕胎。

sentences.en: The phone lines burned up calling all my sisters.
sentences.zh: 电话线都打热了，给我的所有姐妹们打了电话。

sentences.en: Do you know mother's pro-choice?
sentences.zh: 你知道妈妈支持堕胎吗？

sentences.en: This is what she said.
sentences.zh: 她是这么说的。

sentences.en: My mother was so funny.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈太有趣了。

sentences.en: She said, darling, I would have still been having babies.
sentences.zh: 她说，亲爱的，如果你们的姐妹不出面，最大的几个姐妹告诉医生做点什么，我本来还会一直生孩子的。

sentences.en: Had your sisters not stepped in, the oldest sisters told the doctor to do something.
sentences.zh: 而她对此没有意见。

sentences.en: And she was fine with it.
sentences.zh: 她只是不能成为那个告诉他们去做这件事的人。

sentences.en: She just couldn't be the one to tell them to do it.
sentences.zh: 为什么你要在这个州访问这家堕胎诊所并与这位主任交谈？

sentences.en: And why are you visiting this abortion clinic in this state and speaking to this director?
sentences.zh: 嗯，路易斯安那州确实是各州试图监管甚至消除堕胎的绝对核心地带。

sentences.en: Well, Louisiana really is ground zero for state efforts to regulate, if not eliminate, abortion.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州已经颁布了89项不同的堕胎限制措施。

sentences.en: Louisiana has enacted 89 different abortion restrictions.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得真正有趣的是……

sentences.en: But what I find really interesting...
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 就一张，就一张。

sentences.en: Just one, just one.
sentences.zh: 但这是医师和超声波技师必须与患者一起审查的表格。

sentences.en: But this is the form the physician and sonographer must review with the patient.
sentences.zh: 我也要把这个交给你。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you this as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，在路易斯安那州经营一家堕胎诊所意味着，正如凯瑟琳向我展示的那样，你必须字面意义上翻阅厚厚一叠规章制度，只为了确保自己能继续营业。

sentences.en: So to be an abortion clinic in Louisiana means you have to literally, as Kathleen showed me, leaf through a sheaf of regulations just to make sure you can stay open.
sentences.zh: 它们涵盖了诸如24小时等待期、要求堕胎提供者向患者宣读

sentences.en: And they cover things like 24-hour waiting periods, requirements that abortion providers read their
sentences.zh: 胎儿描述、可能发生的并发症、向她们展示超声波图像等规定。

sentences.en: patients' descriptions of the fetus, the complications that might happen, show them sonograMs.

sentences.en: They can look away if they wish.
sentences.zh: 允许她们听胎儿心跳。

sentences.en: Allow them to hear fetal heartbeats.

sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，就我的目的而言，我在那里是为了评估一项法律的影响，该法律要求堕胎提供者、

sentences.en: But most importantly, for my purposes, I was there to assess the impact of a law that requires abortion providers,
sentences.zh: 提供堕胎服务的医生必须在附近的医院拥有收治特权。

sentences.en: doctors who provide abortions, to have admitting privileges at nearby hospitals.
sentences.zh: 再跟我多讲讲那项法律。

sentences.en: And tell me a little bit more about that law.
sentences.zh: 所以这项法律，当你第一次听说它时，听起来非常通情达理。

sentences.en: So this law, when you first hear about it, sounds perfectly sensible.
sentences.zh: 路易斯安那州是第五个通过法律要求堕胎医生在附近医院拥有收治特权的州。

sentences.en: Louisiana is the fifth state to adopt a law that requires abortion doctors to have admitting privileges at a nearby hospital.
sentences.zh: 它于2014年颁布。

sentences.en: It was enacted in 2014.
sentences.zh: 支持者表示这让医疗保健更安全。

sentences.en: Supporters say they make health care safer.
sentences.zh: 议员们表示，这是一项保护女性健康的努力，它是一种资质认证职能。

sentences.en: Lawmakers say that it was an effort to protect women's health, that it's a kind of credentialing function.
sentences.zh: 反对者则表示，整件事都是个幌子，堕胎是一项非常安全的手术，

sentences.en: Opponents say the whole thing is a ruse, that abortion is a very safe procedure,
sentences.zh: 无论你的医生是否有收治特权，在极少数出现并发症需要入院的情况下，你都会被收入院，

sentences.en: that you'll be admitted to the hospital on the very rare occasions that there are complications whether your doctor has admitting privileges or not,
sentences.zh: 而且要获得收治特权是很困难的。

sentences.en: and that it's hard to get admitting privileges.
sentences.zh: 出于政治原因，许多医院不想授予堕胎提供者收治特权。

sentences.en: Many hospitals don't want to give abortion providers admitting privileges for political reasons.
sentences.zh: 这些相互冲突的观点正是一起已上诉至最高法院的案件的核心，最高法院将裁决路易斯安那州的这项堕胎监管规定是否符合宪法。

sentences.en: And those conflicting views are at the center of a case that has reached the Supreme Court, which will decide whether this Louisiana abortion regulation is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 如果最高法院对你们作出不利裁决，这家诊所就会关闭，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: If the Supreme Court rules against you, this clinic closes, you think?
sentences.zh: 很有可能。

sentences.en: Very possibly.
sentences.zh: 那这对该州这一地区的女性意味着什么？

sentences.en: And what does that mean for the women in this part of the state?
sentences.zh: 我们距离可能幸存的任何诊所有多远？

sentences.en: How far are we from whatever clinics might remain?
sentences.zh: 最少四个小时。

sentences.en: Minimum four hours.
sentences.zh: 对一些女性来说，这让她们望尘莫及。

sentences.en: And for some women, that puts it out of reach.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，我们在这里合作的大多数女性生活在联邦贫困线或以下。

sentences.en: You have to understand, most of the women we work with here live at or below the federal poverty level.
sentences.zh: 她们寻求终止妊娠的全部原因在于，她们已经在努力照顾现有的家庭了。

sentences.en: The whole reason they're looking, seeking to terminate a pregnancy is they're already trying to take care of the families they have.
sentences.zh: 她们再也无法承受更多的负担了。

sentences.en: They can't add to that anymore.
sentences.zh: 诊所曾表示，尽管他们有一名拥有收治特权的医生，

sentences.en: The clinic has said that although they have one doctor with admitting privileges,
sentences.zh: 但该医生无法承担诊所的全部工作负荷，诊所很可能不得不关闭。

sentences.en: that doctor cannot carry the whole load of the clinic, and the clinic would very likely have to close.
sentences.zh: 亚当，关于收治特权、堕胎和最高法院的这个问题，听起来非常耳熟。

sentences.en: Adam, this question of admitting privileges and abortion and the Supreme Court, it has a very familiar ring to it.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it should.
sentences.zh: 今晚我们从一代人中关于堕胎的最全面裁决开始报道。

sentences.en: We begin tonight with the most sweeping decision on abortion in a generation.
sentences.zh: 今天，最高法院推翻了一项对诊所和医生施加严格要求的得克萨斯州法律。

sentences.en: Today, the Supreme Court struck down a Texas law that imposed strict requirements on clinics and doctors.
sentences.zh: 得克萨斯州的堕胎法要求堕胎诊所的医生获得附近医院的收治特权。

sentences.en: The Texas abortion law requiring doctors at abortion clinics to get admitting privileges at nearby hospitals.
sentences.zh: 最高法院已经在2016年审理一起相同的得克萨斯州法律时对此问题作出了裁决。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court has already decided this question in the context of an identical Texas law in 2016.
sentences.zh: 法院推翻了得克萨斯州的法律。

sentences.en: The court struck down the Texas law.
sentences.zh: 支持堕胎的一方欢欣鼓舞，而反堕胎势力则陷入绝望。

sentences.en: Jubilation from the pro-choice side, but despair from anti-abortion forces.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅仅几年后，它又开始审视来自另一个州——路易斯安那州的相同法律，这可能会让一些人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So it might be surprising to some that just a few years later, it's taking a look at an identical law from a different state from Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 是的，既然已经有了先例，为什么法院还要审视完全相同的问题？

sentences.en: Yeah, why would the court be looking at the exact same question if there is a precedent?
sentences.zh: 而先例就是那项得克萨斯州法律违宪。

sentences.en: And the precedent is that that Texas law is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 嗯，出乎许多人意料的是，一个联邦上诉法院维持了该法律的效力，尽管来自得克萨斯州几乎相同的法规已被宣布违宪。

sentences.en: Well, to the surprise of many, a federal appeals court had upheld the law, even though a nearly identical statute from Texas was declared unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 一个联邦上诉法院维持了路易斯安那州的法律，这意味着最高法院几乎别无选择，只能受理此案。

sentences.en: A federal appeals court sustained the Louisiana law, meaning the Supreme Court almost had no choice but to take this case.
sentences.zh: 因为无论法院本身可能对收治特权法律做些什么，

sentences.en: Because whatever the court might want to do itself about admitting privileges laws,
sentences.zh: 一个联邦巡回法院开辟新领域，并且在某些人看来无视该领域看似具有约束力的最高法院先例，这似乎有点奇怪。

sentences.en: it seems a little odd for a federal circuit court to be breaking new ground and in the eyes of some to disregard what looks like binding Supreme Court precedent in this area.
sentences.zh: 为什么下级法院会公开违抗一项针对相同法律、已有四年历史的最高法院先例？

sentences.en: And why would a lower court openly defy a four-year-old Supreme Court precedent on an identical law?
sentences.zh: 这有点说不通。

sentences.en: That doesn't make a whole lot of sense.

sentences.en: They said that they were able to discern differences between Louisiana and Texas.

sentences.en: They say that the abortion providers didn't try hard enough in Louisiana to get admitting privileges.

sentences.en: And more importantly, a lot has changed since 2016.
sentences.zh: 在该任期最后一天之后，我们刚刚获悉安东尼·肯尼迪大法官即将退休。

sentences.en: After the final day of the term, we have just learned that Justice Anthony Kennedy will be retiring.
sentences.zh: 最高法院，这就是全部的意义所在。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court, it's what it's all about.
sentences.zh: 我将要任命的大法官将是反堕胎的。

sentences.en: The justices that I'm going to appoint will be pro-life.
sentences.zh: 他们将具有保守倾向。

sentences.en: A lot has changed since President Trump put a lot of new judges on the courts, the lower courts and the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里是为了庆祝历史。

sentences.en: We are here to celebrate history.

sentences.zh: 美国最高法院的最新成员，布雷特·卡瓦诺大法官。

sentences.zh: 各州立法机构的情况发生了很大变化，它们正在接连颁布堕胎限制令。

sentences.en: A lot has changed in state legislatures, which are enacting abortion restriction after abortion restriction.

sentences.en: Folks opposed to abortion are very hopeful that we live in a different judicial climate and that this new Supreme Court might take a very different view of abortion rights than earlier ones had.

sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 新闻。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是《纽约时报》的订阅用户，请立即下载时报App，即可免费畅享30天。

sentences.en: We'll hear argument this morning, case 181323, June Medical Services versus Russo, and the cross petition 181460, Russell versus June Medical Services.
sentences.zh: 今天上午我们将听取辩论，案号为18-1323，“琼医疗服务诉鲁索案”，以及交叉上诉案18-1460，“罗素诉琼医疗服务案”。

sentences.en: Okay, so Adam, tell us what happened inside the Supreme Court last week as this case opens up.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚当，请跟我们讲讲上周此案开庭时，最高法院内部发生了什么。

sentences.en: It was a little hard to make sense of what was going on at the court.
sentences.zh: 要弄清楚法院当时在发生什么有点困难。

sentences.en: You know for sure that the court's four more liberal members are completely on board with striking down this law.
sentences.zh: 你可以确信，法院中那四位偏自由派的成员完全赞成推翻这项法律。

sentences.en: They think the 2016 Texas case takes care of it, but they also think if they were looking at this fresh,
sentences.zh: 他们认为2016年的得克萨斯州案已经解决了这个问题，但他们也认为，如果从头审视此案，

sentences.en: this is a regulation that they say confers no medical benefits, but imposes enormous costs on women's ability to obtain abortions.
sentences.zh: 他们会认为这是一项既没有带来任何医疗益处，却给女性堕胎能力施加了沉重成本的法规。

sentences.en: So you could hear this intense skepticism as the more liberal justices ask questions.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着偏自由派的大法官们提出质问，你能听到这种强烈的怀疑态度。

sentences.en: Justice Elena Kagan, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如埃лена·卡根大法官。

sentences.en: Is it right that there is evidence in the record that Hope Clinic has served over 3,000 women annually for 23 years,
sentences.zh: 记录中是否有证据表明，“希望诊所”23年来每年为3000多名女性服务，

sentences.en: so that's around 70,000 women, and has transferred only four patients ever to a hospital?
sentences.zh: 也就是大约7万名女性，而历史上总共只有4名患者被转诊到医院？

sentences.en: She did the math.
sentences.zh: 她算了一下账。

sentences.en: She said it amounted to some 70,000 abortions, and they had complications necessitating trips to the hospital four times.
sentences.zh: 她说这相当于大约7万例堕胎，而其中只有4次因出现并发症而需要去医院。

sentences.en: They know whether they've transferred women to a hospital, and it's four.
sentences.zh: 他们很清楚自己是否将女性转诊到过医院，数字就是4。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know of a medical procedure where it's lower than that of any kind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，据我所知，没有任何一种医疗程序的转诊率比这更低了。

sentences.en: And so Kagan's point is women so rarely need to be admitted to hospitals that there's no rationale for requiring admitting privileges for abortion practitioners in these clinics.
sentences.zh: 所以卡根的观点是，女性极少需要入院，因此要求这些诊所的堕胎执业医生具备住院特权根本没有合理的依据。

sentences.en: That was her point.
sentences.zh: 这就是她的观点。

sentences.en: If indeed having admitting privileges makes it more likely that you'll be able to go to the hospital, but that itself is a contested proposition.
sentences.zh: 如果说拥有住院特权确实能让你更有可能去医院，但这一点本身就是一个备受争议的命题。

sentences.en: There's no real link between your doctor having admitting privileges and you getting the medical care you need at a hospital.
sentences.zh: 你的医生拥有住院特权与你在医院获得所需的医疗护理之间，并没有真正的联系。

sentences.en: What about the other liberal justices?
sentences.zh: 其他自由派大法官呢？

sentences.en: Justice Sotomayor raised a different question, whether some doctors, because of the nature of their practices, could ever get hospital admitting privileges.
sentences.zh: 索托马约尔大法官提出了一个不同的问题，即某些医生是否由于其业务性质，而永远无法获得医院住院特权。

sentences.en: She talked about a doctor who doesn't perform surgical abortions, but only so-called medication abortions where patients are given pills.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了一位不实施手术流产，而只实施所谓的药物流产（即向患者提供药丸）的医生。

sentences.en: And that kind of doctor, she said, could never get admitting privileges in Louisiana, and so would be prohibited from performing abortions entirely.
sentences.zh: 她说，这种医生在路易斯安那州永远无法获得住院特权，因此将被彻底禁止实施堕胎。

sentences.en: Adam, I have to imagine that some of these liberal justices also raised the simple question of precedent from that Texas case in 2016.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我猜这些自由派大法官中，也有人提出了2016年得州那个案子中关于判例的简单问题。

sentences.en: Justice Breyer, I have read the briefs, I understand there are good arguments on both sides.
sentences.zh: 布雷耶大法官，我读过简报，我知道双方都有很好的论点。

sentences.en: Indeed, in the country, people have very strong feelings, and a lot of people morally think it's wrong, and a lot of people morally think the opposite is wrong.
sentences.zh: 确实，在全国范围内，人们有着非常强烈的感受，许多人从道德上认为这是错的，而许多人从道德上认为恰恰相反的事才是错的。

sentences.en: The court is struggling with the problem of what kind of rule of law do you have in a country that contains both sorts of people.
sentences.zh: 法院正在艰难解决这样一个问题：在一个同时包含这两种人的国家里，究竟应该实行什么样的法治规则？

sentences.en: He paused and said, listen, people have very strong feelings about the issue of abortion.
sentences.zh: 他停顿了一下说，听着，人们对堕胎问题有着极其强烈的感受。

sentences.en: People have moral objections to it.
sentences.zh: 人们对此有道德上的反对意见。

sentences.en: People believe that women have a right to it.
sentences.zh: 人们坚信女性拥有这项权利。

sentences.en: But why depart from what was pretty clear precedent?
sentences.zh: 但为什么要背离相当清晰的既定判例呢？

sentences.en: And the job for the court is to hold the nation together under the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 法院的职责是在法治之下将国家凝聚在一起。

sentences.en: And the way to do that, he said, was to respect precedent.
sentences.zh: 他说，实现这一目标的方法就是尊重判例。

sentences.en: And what is the response from the lawyers defending the law to that question of precedent?
sentences.zh: 面对关于判例的这个问题，捍卫该法律的律师作何回应？

sentences.en: They say Louisiana is different.
sentences.zh: 他们说路易斯安那州的情况不同。

sentences.en: They basically say our admitting privileges law, we have a different justification for it than the one put forward by Texas, this credentialing justification.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是说，对于我们的住院特权法，我们有着与得州提出的不同的辩护理由，即这种资质认证的理由。

sentences.en: And we also think the impact in Louisiana is going to be different.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还认为路易斯安那州受到的影响会有所不同。

sentences.en: In Texas, the fear was that the state would go from 40 abortion clinics to 10 in an enormous geographically vast state.
sentences.zh: 在得克萨斯州，人们担心在一个地域极其辽阔的州里，诊所数量会从40家锐减至10家。

sentences.en: Here they say there's no special reason to think it should go from three to one because they say if only doctors tried harder to get admitting privileges, they probably could.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，他们说没有特别的理由认为它会从3家变成1家，因为他们说如果医生们更努力地去争取住院特权，他们很可能是能做到的。

sentences.en: So their point is maybe the words of the law are the same, but the facts on the ground are different.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的观点是，也许法律条文是一样的，但实地情况是不同的。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，律师。

sentences.en: OK, that was the liberal side of the court.
sentences.zh: 好的，那是法院自由派的一面。

sentences.en: What did you see, Adam, from the conservative justices here who it seems will ultimately decide this case?
sentences.zh: 亚当，从看来最终将裁决此案的保守派大法官身上，你看到了什么？

sentences.en: The right side of the court was unusually hard to read.
sentences.zh: 法院右翼的意图极其难猜。

sentences.en: Let's take one example.
sentences.zh: 我们举个例子。

sentences.en: Let's take Doe No.
sentences.zh: 我们以“2号匿名字原告”为例。

sentences.en: Doe No.
sentences.zh: 2号匿名字原告是本案的原告，对吧？

sentences.en: 2 is plaintiff in this case, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，尊敬的法官。

sentences.en: Yes, Your Honor.
sentences.zh: 唯一一位对代表堕胎服务提供者的律师不断提出敌意问题的法官是塞缪尔·阿利托。

sentences.en: The only justice who asked consistently hostile questions of the lawyer representing the abortion providers was Samuel Alito.
sentences.zh: 他作证说，他没有在那里申请住院特权，因为那是一家天主教医院。

sentences.en: He testified that he didn't apply for admitting privileges there because it's a Catholic hospital.
sentences.zh: 难道不是吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 那是证词的一部分。

sentences.en: That was part of the testimony.
sentences.zh: 而且他的语气非常强硬。

sentences.en: And he came on strong.
sentences.zh: 当2号匿名字原告解释他为什么没有向这家医院申请时，他部分原因地表示，因为那不是一个让我觉得舒适的地方。

sentences.en: When Doe No.
sentences.zh: 他难道不是这么说的吗？

sentences.en: 2 explained why he didn't apply to this hospital, he said in part because it's not a place where I would feel comfortable.
sentences.zh: 他是这么说的，尊敬的法官。

sentences.en: Didn't he say that?
sentences.zh: 但他却是唯一一个态度强硬的人。

sentences.en: He did, Your Honor.
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯一如既往地没有提出任何问题。

sentences.en: But he was the only one who came on strong.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统的第一位最高法院提名人尼尔·戈萨奇大法官，在口头辩论中通常很活跃。

sentences.en: Clarence Thomas, as is his custom, asked no questions.
sentences.zh: 但令我和许多人惊讶的是，他在这次辩论中一言不发。

sentences.en: Justice Neil Gorsuch, President Trump's first appointee, is usually active at oral argument.
sentences.zh: 这让人很难知道他的立场可能会倾向于哪一边。

sentences.en: And to my surprise and the surprise of many, he said nothing at all during this argument.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Making it very difficult to know where he may be leaning.
sentences.zh: 他相当保守。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 我不得不认为他并不认为存在宪法层面的堕胎权。

sentences.en: He's quite conservative.
sentences.zh: 但并没有太多的司法履历可以用来支撑这种直觉。

sentences.en: I have to think he doesn't think there's a constitutional right to abortion.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在法院的第二位提名人卡瓦诺大法官呢？

sentences.en: But there's not a lot of judicial track record to pin that intuition on.
sentences.zh: 卡瓦诺大法官提出的问题似乎展现出一种思想开放的姿态，试图厘清本案中的各种争议问题。

sentences.en: What about President Trump's second appointee on the court, Justice Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 例如，他想知道，如果有一项法规可能对促进女性健康没有任何作用，

sentences.en: Justice Kavanaugh asked questions that seemed to show an open-minded attempt to sort through the various issues in the case.
sentences.zh: 但也没有增加她们堕胎的困难，那么这样的法规是否可行？

sentences.en: He wanted to know, for instance, whether a regulation that maybe didn't do anything to further women's health,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果一个州通过了一项住院特权法，假设某个州有10家诊所，每家诊所有两名医生，

sentences.en: but also didn't make it harder for them to have abortions, whether such a regulation would be possible.
sentences.zh: 但全部20名医生都能轻易获得住院特权，从而对诊所没有影响，

sentences.en: If a state passed an admitting privileges law, therefore, and suppose a state had 10 clinics and two doctors for each clinic,
sentences.zh: 对实施堕胎的医生没有影响，因此对获得堕胎服务的女性也没有影响，那么在该州这样的法律是否符合宪法？

sentences.en: but all 20 doctors could easily get the admitting privileges so that there'd be no effect on the clinics,
sentences.zh: 所以他假设性地问道，如果每个诊所的每个医生都能获得住院特权，我们是否仍然必须推翻这项法律？

sentences.en: no effect on the doctors who perform abortions, and therefore no effect on the women who obtain abortions, would a law be constitutional in that state?
sentences.zh: 这其实是在抛出这样一个问题：我们是否必须受制于当年的得州裁决，还是我们可以认定同一条法律在不同地方会产生不同的影响？

sentences.en: So he asked, hypothetically, what if every doctor in every clinic was able to get admitting privileges, would we still have to strike down that law?
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管卡瓦诺大法官听起来思想开明，但他在担任联邦上诉法院法官期间的一些司法裁决表明，

sentences.en: And that was a way of asking the question of, are we bound by that Texas decision, or can we find that the same law with the same words has a different impact in a different place?
sentences.zh: 他对堕胎权并不感冒，例如曾投票阻止一名怀孕的无证移民少女去堕胎。

sentences.en: But as open-minded as Justice Kavanaugh sounded, there is some evidence in his judicial rulings when he was a federal appeals court judge
sentences.zh: 听起来有理由相信你提到的这四位法官——阿利托、托马斯、戈萨奇、卡瓦诺，他们可能都会支持路易斯安那州的这项法律。

sentences.en: that he is not comfortable with abortion rights, voting, for instance, to block a pregnant undocumented teen from being able to get an abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会投票支持维持原判。

sentences.en: So it sounds like there's reason to believe that these four justices you have mentioned, Alito, Thomas, Gorsuch, Kavanaugh, they may all support this Louisiana law.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是我们掌握的最好信息：四位自由派立场坚定，你提到的四位保守派也相当坚定，这就剩下一位大法官了。

sentences.en: They might vote to uphold it.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's the best information we have, that the four liberals are solid, that the four conservatives you mentioned are pretty solid, and that leaves one justice.
sentences.zh: 是的，他在各种案件中越来越多地发现自己处于法院意识形态的中心。

sentences.en: Chief Justice John Roberts.
sentences.zh: 那么约翰·罗伯茨在这些口头辩论中的表现如何？

sentences.en: Yes, who more and more finds himself at the ideological center of the court in all kinds of cases.
sentences.zh: 你是否同意，在任何案件中，无论我们讨论的是哪个州，根据法律进行的“益处审查”都将是相同的？

sentences.en: And what is John Roberts' conduct during these oral arguments?
sentences.zh: 所以在这个案子里，他的立场非常难猜。

sentences.en: Do you agree that the benefits inquiry under the law is going to be the same in every case, regardless of which state we're talking about?
sentences.zh: 但你需要了解的是：

sentences.en: So he's very hard to read in this case.
sentences.zh: 在2016年的那个案件中，即涉及得克萨斯州的案件中，他曾表示得州的法律没有问题。

sentences.en: But here's what you need to know.
sentences.zh: 他当时投票支持维持得州的法律。

sentences.en: In the 2016 case, in the case involving Texas, he said the Texas law was fine.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很有意思。

sentences.en: He voted to uphold the Texas law.
sentences.zh: 现在他面对的是一模一样的路易斯安那州法律。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 他甚至愿意对此保持开放心态，这本身就可能是一个巨大的惊喜。

sentences.en: And now he's looking at the identical Louisiana law.
sentences.zh: 我理解这种观点，即法律的影响因州而异。

sentences.en: And for him even to be open-minded about it might be a big surprise.
sentences.zh: 但既然法律带来的益处不会因州而异，为什么你要对每个州区别看待呢？

sentences.en: And I understand the point that the impact of the laws varies from state to state.
sentences.zh: 他接连提出了一系列问题，对路易斯安那州的法律似乎抱有几分怀疑。

sentences.en: But why do you look at each state differently if the benefits of the law, they're not going to change from state to state?
sentences.zh: 他似乎接受了这样一种观点，即它可能并没有为女性带来任何医疗益处。

sentences.en: He asks a series of questions that seem a little skeptical about the Louisiana law.
sentences.zh: 它可能并未保护她们的健康。

sentences.en: He seems to be buying the idea that it may not confer any medical benefits to women.
sentences.zh: 这使这位首席大法官处在了一个非常耐人寻味的聚光灯下。

sentences.en: It may not protect their health.
sentences.zh: 所以，四年前首席大法官罗伯茨曾投票支持过一模一样的得州法律。

sentences.en: And that casts the chief justice in a very interesting light.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在对律师的提问中，他似乎对路易斯安那州相同的法律持怀疑态度，甚至可能有点倾向于将其推翻。

sentences.en: So Chief Justice Roberts was a vote in favor of this identical Texas law four years ago.
sentences.zh: 因此，首席大法官罗伯茨经常面临相互冲突的内心理念。

sentences.en: And now, in his questions to the lawyers, he seems skeptical of the identical law in Louisiana, perhaps somewhat open to striking it down.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是个保守派。

sentences.en: So Chief Justice Roberts often has conflicting impulses.
sentences.zh: 他是保守派法律运动的产物。

sentences.en: He's basically conservative.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也是法院廉洁与权威的守护者。

sentences.en: He's a product of the conservative legal movement.
sentences.zh: 他可能会想，听着，这个问题我们已经裁决过一次了。

sentences.en: But he's also the steward of the court's integrity and authority.
sentences.zh: 一个联邦上诉法院似乎无视了我们。

sentences.en: And he may think that, listen, we've decided this question once.
sentences.zh: 这是不可接受的。

sentences.en: A federal appeals court seems to have ignored us.
sentences.zh: 即便我第一次可能会投出不同的票，但这里还有其他利益在起作用。

sentences.en: That's not acceptable.
sentences.zh: 如果没有其他问题了。

sentences.en: And even though I might have voted differently the first time, there are other interests at play here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢各位律师。

sentences.en: If there are no further questions.
sentences.zh: 本案现已结案呈交。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 那么你认为这一切最终会如何收场？

sentences.en: The case is submitted.
sentences.zh: 你在预测最高法院案件结果方面的记录好得惊人。

sentences.en: So how do you think this all will shake out?
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，我感到很困惑。

sentences.en: You have an almost startlingly good track record of predicting outcomes in Supreme Court cases.
sentences.zh: 我真的不认为约翰·罗伯茨愿意养成这样一种习惯：通过5比4的投票结果与法院的自由派站在一起。

sentences.en: I'm confused, Michael.
sentences.zh: 但我想我确实认为存在这样一类案件——这或许就是其中之一——其中对法治、判例以及司法廉洁的尊崇理念，

sentences.en: I really don't think that John Roberts wants to make it a habit of having five, four decisions in which he joins the court's liberals.
sentences.zh: 可能会把他推向那个让他感到不舒服的方向。

sentences.en: But I guess I do think that there's a class of cases, and this may be one of them, where a conception of respect for the rule of law and for precedent and for judicial integrity
sentences.zh: 走向自由派并推翻这项法律。

sentences.en: might push him in that uncomfortable direction.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Towards the liberals and striking down this law.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我很好奇。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳对这里将发生的事情有什么看法？

sentences.en: Adam, I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 她非常非常紧张。

sentences.en: What does Kathleen say about what she thinks will happen here?
sentences.zh: 她认为在过去的几年里，全景、法律、社会和政治环境已经转向了对堕胎权不利的方向。

sentences.en: She is very, very nervous.
sentences.zh: 她对自己的诊所的未来感到紧张。

sentences.en: She thinks that in the past couple of years, the landscape, the legal, social, political landscape has shifted against abortion rights.
